title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 89
paragraphs: Artabazos son of Pharnakes, meanwhile, in his flight from Plataea was by now getting well on his way. When he came to the Thessalians, they offered him hospitality and asked about the rest of the army, knowing nothing of what had happened at Plataea. Artabazos, knowing that if he told them the whole truth about the fighting, he would run the risk of being destroyed both himself and the whole army with him (for he thought they would all attack him once informed of what had happened), reflecting on this, had told nothing of it to the Phokians, and now to the Thessalians he said: “I, as you see, Thessalians, am eager to march by the shortest way to Thrace; I am in great haste, having been sent with these men on a certain business from the army. Mardonius himself and his army are to be expected here shortly, marching close after me. Give him entertainment and show yourselves serviceable, for you will not in the end repent having done so.” Having said this, he continued to march his army with haste through Thessaly and Macedonia straight for Thrace, truly eager to press on and going through the country by the shortest possible way. So he came to Byzantion, having left behind him great numbers of his army — either cut down on the way by the Thracians or overcome by hunger and fatigue — and from Byzantion he crossed over in ships. Thus he himself made his return to Asia.
